title: emergencyWithdraw skips _recomputeSchedule/_updatePool, leaving stale rewardRate that over-emits the reward budget to surviving stakers
plausibility: Plausible Medium (value-leak). The deliberate-extraction variant is Implausible-High only — gated on a post-exit inactivity window the attacker cannot control.
description: emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked (L545) but calls neither _updatePool nor _recomputeSchedule and never advances lastRewardTime. rewardRate therefore stays sized for the pre-exit (larger) pool while totalStaked has shrunk. The next _updatePool (fired by any later stake/unstake/claim via _syncBudget, or by topUp/setTargetAPY) settles elapsed * R_old over the SMALLER totalStaked, inflating accRewardPerShare for survivors by oldTotal/newTotal across the entire [lastRewardTime, now] window (PoC: 1000 -> 10 = 100x). This re-introduces the participation multiplier that the M-03 'no participation multiplier' Critical Invariant explicitly forbids.
impact: Over-emission of the protocol reward budget (real phUSD allocated for emissions) vs the targetAPY policy, redistributed to whoever remains staked. NOT user principal (emergencyWithdraw returns principal in full) and NOT insolvency: the solvency invariant balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt holds throughout (PoC-confirmed; over-draw hard-clamped to rewardBudget at NFTStaker.sol:329). Impact = mis-emission / runway drain (loss of in-motion emissions), capped at Medium by the loss-of-yield rule. Two variants: (a) non-malicious — any legitimate large emergency exit silently gifts a runway-draining windfall to remaining stakers; (b) self-profit — attacker holds a large recoverable position + a small side position, emergency-exits the large one (principal returned), waits an inactivity window, then claims ~the budget over the tiny remaining pool.
attackPath: 1. emergencyWithdraw decrements totalStaked (L545) but calls neither _updatePool nor _recomputeSchedule, and does not advance lastRewardTime.
2. rewardRate stays sized for the pre-exit (larger) pool while totalStaked has shrunk.

3. The next _updatePool (fired by any later stake/unstake/claim via _syncBudget, or topUp/setTargetAPY) settles elapsed * R_old over the SMALLER totalStaked, inflating accRewardPerShare for survivors by oldTotal/newTotal across the whole [lastRewardTime, now] window (PoC: 1000 -> 10 = 100x).
4a. Non-malicious: ANY legitimate large emergency exit silently gifts a runway-draining windfall to remaining stakers.

4b. Self-profit variant: attacker holds a large RECOVERABLE position + a small side position, emergency-exits the large one (principal returned), waits an inactivity window, then claims ~the budget over the tiny remaining pool.
recommendation: Call _updatePool() (settle accrual at the OLD rate against the OLD totalStaked) and then _recomputeSchedule() inside emergencyWithdraw AFTER decrementing totalStaked, mirroring the unstake() head+tail pattern. To preserve the escape-hatch guarantee (must not depend on a working dispatcher hook / minter / recompute), gate the recompute in a try/catch or balance-only path so a broken external call can never trap principal — keep principal return unconditional, but refresh rate/lastRewardTime on the success path so survivors cannot inherit the stale high rate.

poc.validatedResult: PASS (2/2); written GREEN (asserts the vulnerable outcome)
poc.result: 100x over-emission demonstrated; solvency invariant PASSES (value-leak, not insolvency); M-03 / runway invariants FAIL

severityDispute.highArgument: Over-emission begins on the very next _updatePool, even a single block is over-emitted, and the leaked funds are real protocol phUSD redistributed to a self-controllable survivor position with recoverable capital -> looks like a direct-loss path.
severityDispute.mediumArgument: No principal theft and no insolvency (solvency holds at all times, over-draw clamped to rewardBudget, principal always returned); the value at risk is in-motion emissions (Medium ceiling per loss-of-yield rule); the value-meaningful drain depends on a stated external requirement (post-exit inactivity) the attacker cannot guarantee; the no-assumption slice is dust-scale one-block over-emission.
severityDispute.resolution: MEDIUM. The no-hypothetical slice is dust-scale; the dramatic PoC drain requires the inactivity external requirement -> 'value leak with stated assumptions + external requirements' Medium definition. Firmly above QA: breaks a stated Critical Invariant AND leaks real value via a core, expected-to-be-used function.
